episodes.title: Tip-Apex Distance < 25 mm
episodes.source: Baumgaertner MR et al. JBJS Am 1995;77(7):1058-64

crosspost.note: YouTube failed at 18:00 (title contained <); rescheduled YouTube alone 18:20

carousel.headline: TAD < 25 mm
carousel.sub: The number that saves your lag screw
points: TAD = tip-to-apex distance on AP + lateral X-rays, corrected for magnification
None of 120 screws with TAD of 25 mm or less cut out
Mean TAD: 24 mm in healed fractures vs 38 mm in cut-outs

episodes.title: Acute compartment syndrome: Delta P < 30 mmHg
episodes.source: McQueen & Court-Brown JBJS Br 1996;78(1):99-104; Kakar et al. JOT 2007;21(2):99-103
episodes.music: track02 (Content ID claim on YouTube: blocked worldwide); YouTube re-uploaded 2026-10-20 11:00 with track01

carousel.headline: ΔP < 30 mmHg
carousel.sub: The number that decides a fasciotomy
points: ΔP = diastolic BP minus intracompartmental pressure
Don't rely on absolute compartment pressure alone
Palpable pulses do NOT exclude compartment syndrome
carousel.ref: McQueen & Court-Brown, JBJS Br 1996 · Kakar et al., JOT 2007

episodes.title: Kocher criteria: septic arthritis vs transient synovitis of the hip in children
episodes.source_hint: Kocher MS et al. JBJS Am 1999 (4 predictors: non-weight-bearing, fever >38.5 C, ESR >40, WBC >12,000; probability by number of predictors); validation Kocher 2004; CRP >2.0 mg/dL added by Caird 2006
episodes.source: Kocher MS et al. JBJS Am 1999;81(12):1662-70; Kocher MS et al. JBJS Am 2004;86(8):1629-35; Caird MS et al. JBJS Am 2006;88(6):1251-7

carousel.headline: KOCHER 4
points: Fever history, non-weight-bearing, ESR at least 40, WBC over 12,000
3 of 4 predictors = 93.1% septic; none = under 0.2%
Add CRP over 2.0 mg/dL (Caird 2006)
carousel.ref: Kocher et al., JBJS Am 1999 · Caird et al., JBJS Am 2006

carousel.headline: OTTAWA 4+4
points: Tender posterior edge/tip of either malleolus (distal 6 cm), 5th MT base or navicular
Or can't bear weight for 4 steps, right after injury and in the ED
Negative LR 0.08: fracture under 1.4% when the rule is negative
carousel.ref: Stiell et al., JAMA 1993 · Bachmann et al., BMJ 2003

carousel.headline: GUSTILO I-III
points: Type I under 1 cm, clean; Type II over 1 cm, no flaps; III high energy
Wound sepsis IIIA 4%, IIIB 52%, IIIC 42% (Gustilo 1984)
Antibiotics after 66 min: OR 3.78 for deep infection (Lack 2015)
carousel.ref: Gustilo et al., J Trauma 1984 · Lack et al., JOT 2015

carousel.headline: 6 HOURS
points: AVN 4.8% if reduced within 6 h vs 52.9% after 6 h
Excellent/good hip at 14 years: 88% vs 42%
Reduced after 12 h: AVN odds ratio 5.6 (meta-analysis)
carousel.ref: Hougaard & Thomsen, Arch Orthop Trauma Surg 1986

carousel.headline: 3 SIGNS
points: Snuffbox, tubercle, thumb compression: each 100% sensitive
All 3 combined within 24 h: specificity 74% (alone 9-48%)
Normal X-ray? MRI most accurate: sens 97.7%, spec 99.8%
carousel.ref: Parvizi et al., J Hand Surg Br 1998

carousel.headline: SALTER-HARRIS
points: Type II most common: 54% of 951 physeal fractures
III & IV break the joint surface: anatomic reduction + fixation
Distal femur: growth disturbance 52%, 58% even in type II
carousel.ref: Basener et al., J Orthop Trauma 2009
